mechanism.rule: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Fuel System Integrity of Hydrogen Vehicles; Compressed Hydrogen Storage System Integrity; Incorporation by Reference (final rule establishing FMVSS No. 307 and FMVSS No. 308)
mechanism.agency: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (U.S. Department of Transportation)
mechanism.required: The rule establishes two new Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards that specify performance requirements for all motor vehicles that use hydrogen as a fuel source. FMVSS No. 307 sets requirements for the integrity of the fuel system in hydrogen vehicles during normal vehicle operations and after crashes. FMVSS No. 308 sets requirements for the compressed hydrogen storage system.
mechanism.benefits: The retrieved text of the final rule gives no dollar or lives-saved figure for benefits. It states that most of the safety benefits of the rule will only be realized when hydrogen vehicles become more prevalent.
mechanism.costs: The retrieved text of the final rule gives no dollar estimate of costs. It states that the rule is nonsignificant under E.O. 12866 and that most manufacturers and vehicle lines currently in production would be unaffected.
mechanism.agency_reasons: NHTSA states that FMVSS Nos. 307 and 308 focus on the fuel system integrity of vehicles that use compressed hydrogen as fuel. The stated purpose is to reduce deaths and injuries from fires caused by hydrogen fuel leakage during vehicle operation and after crashes, and from explosions caused by the bursting of pressurized hydrogen containers.
mechanism.status: S.J.Res.55 (119th Congress) was introduced by Sen. Capito. It passed the Senate without amendment on 2025-05-21 by 51-46 (Record Vote 275). Congress.gov lists the latest action as 'Held at the desk' in the House (2025-05-26). No House passage, presentment to the President or Public Law number was found. On that record the resolution has not become law, so the rule has not been voided by it.

notes: 1) Status: the Senate passed S.J.Res.55 on 2025-05-21 by 51-46. The only record found of any later action is Congress.gov's 'Held at the desk' in the House on 2025-05-26, and the checker cannot open Congress.gov. No Public Law number was found. The status should be re-verified against the Clerk of the House and govinfo Public Laws before publication. 2) Costs and benefits: the rule is classed as nonsignificant under E.O. 12866, and OMB did not review it (per Ballotpedia, which quotes the proposed rule). No regulatory impact analysis with monetized benefits or costs was found. The rule text was read only through search excerpts, not the full document, so the benefits and costs fields say only what those excerpts state. No CBO, GAO or court finding disputing any estimate was found. 3) Sponsor reasons: no statement by Sen. Capito or other supporters on the substance of the hydrogen-vehicle rule was found, so the field is omitted. The Senate record shows the resolution was debated on 2025-05-21 alongside Majority Leader Thune's points of order on CRA procedure. The Hill reported that the resolution would serve as a vehicle to expand the reach of the CRA, and that Thune moved to it first for that reason (https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/5312952-thune-creates-procedure-ev-mandate/). This is reporting, not a sponsor statement of reasons. Sen. Whitehouse is recorded in the Congressional Record as opposing the resolution while noting it was an actual CRA resolution. 4) Outcomes: no official record was found of hydrogen-vehicle crash, leak or injury data after the rule's effective date (2025-07-16). Because the resolution has not been shown to have become law, no harm or burden relief caused by removal of the rule can be recorded. The compliance date of September 1, 2028 appears only in a secondary source (TUV) and is not stated here. 5) The 2026-06-03 amendment outcome is a record of codified text. It does not state whether any vehicle was affected.
